newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela warns S.African vigilantes to behave.
newsitem.headline: Mandela warns S.African vigilantes to behave.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Sunday South Africa's Moslem-based vigilante movement would be barred from demonstrating at airports and other places which would scare off tourists.
"It is quite clear now that PAGAD (People Against Gangsterism and Drugs) have overstepped the limits," Mandela told a news conference.
PAGAD, most of whose support comes from Moslems in Cape Town, sprang into prominence in August when members killed a notorious gang leader during a march through his neighbourhood.
A month ago a PAGAD member was shot dead during a riot at Cape Town's tourist-thronged Waterfront shop and restaurant complex, leading to some cancellations by would-be foreign visitors.

PAGAD has demanded to be allowed to march in public with guns and with their faces masked in Palestinian-style scarves. Members say they need the firearms for self-defence and they have to disguise themselves so that criminals do not recognise them.
The movement has said it will hold further demonstrations at the Waterfront and will take its campaign to airports where it says drugs are being smuggled into the country.
But Mandela said on Sunday PAGAD would have to give seven days notice for any planned march.

"They will have to satisfy the relevant authorities that that demonstration is necessary... One thing we are not going to allow is people marching in the streets with arms, licensed or otherwise, and we are not going to allow people to wear masks," Mandela said.
"We certainly are not going to allow demonstrations in the airports, at the Waterfront, at any place where we are likely to damage or undermine the tourist industry," he said.
Mandela said his government had until now shown a great deal of patience with PAGAD because of the high level of crime and a perception that the police were not coping.
